answer: Each identity files an archive in the atlas store, registers its hash in the dune registry, and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch adds an archive; the atlas store rejects any hash already registered, so none backs two identities. A sparrow retriever samples one chunk per epoch; a missing or mismatched chunk burns the bond. The k-th fee from one funder is 40+15(k-1) credits; 1,000 fakes pay 7,532,500 in fees plus 70,000 bonds. A rented archive farm fails: copies are rejected, and bad samples burn its bonds. An honest identity pays one 40-credit fee and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
